taskVersion.name: ves-heldout-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station H-01, survey area H. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 332.5 | 0.52 | 0.52
2 | 601.3 | 6.89 | 7.41
3 | 359.9 | 16.01 | 23.42
4 | 286.0 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KQ-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station H-01, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Note – Station H-01, Survey Area H**

The interpreted VES model shows four layers. Resistivity increases from 332.5 Ω·m (Layer 1, 0.52 m thick) to a maximum of 601.3 Ω·m (Layer 2, 6.89 m thick), then decreases progressively through 359.9 Ω·m (Layer 3, 16.01 m thick) to 286.0 Ω·m in the basal layer (Layer 4, unbounded).

Applying the three-layer rule:
- Layers 1-2-3: 332.5 < 601.3 > 359.9 → **K**
- Layers 2-3-4: 601.3 > 359.9 > 286.0 → **Q**

This gives a curve type of **KQ**, consistent with the resistivity-depth pattern (rise then steady decline). The on-file classification of KQ-type is confirmed by the layer resistivity values, and no discrepancy is noted. Drilling teams should expect a resistive mid-depth zone (Layer 2) sandwiched between lower-resistivity surface and deeper materials.

{"curve_type_stated": "KQ", "label_issue_flagged": false}
